name: ElevateDB
tagline: Royalty-free embedded and client/server SQL engine for Delphi, C++Builder, Lazarus, .NET, ODBC and PHP apps.
description: ElevateDB is a commercial relational engine from Elevate Software of North Tonawanda, New York, launched in 2007 as the successor to the company's DBISAM, which had replaced the Borland Database Engine in many Delphi applications. It implements a large subset of SQL:2003, including views, triggers, SQL/PSM stored procedures and functions, constraints, generated and computed columns and intervals, and also gives Delphi developers fast navigational, table-cursor access. The same client code works against local single-user files or the ElevateDB Server, a single executable whose source is included with some editions. It is licensed per developer with royalty-free redistribution and is still maintained: 2.40 added RAD Studio 13 support in September 2025, followed by Build 3 that October.

pricing.notes: Licensed per developer with royalty-free runtime distribution; the first year of updates is included, then an optional subscription.

scale.notes: Built for packaged applications: local files or a single ElevateDB Server, with store-based replication between sites.

strengths: Royalty-free distribution: no per-install database licence to pass on to customers
Same client code switches between embedded single-user files and multi-user client/server
Tight Delphi/C++Builder/Lazarus integration with both SQL and navigational table access
Server source code available, so ISVs can rebrand or customise it
Still tracking new RAD Studio releases (RAD Studio 13 support in 2025)
weaknesses: Ecosystem is centred on Delphi; few tools or hosting options elsewhere
No clustering, sharding or managed cloud offering
Small vendor; support is mainly forums and the founder's team
useCases: Packaged Delphi or C++Builder business applications (POS, practice management, pharmacy)
Replacing BDE/Paradox or DBISAM back ends
Desktop apps that need to grow from single-user to client/server without code changes
